Comparisons across ocean basins will distinguish shared responses from local seasonality and site-specific conditions.</p><p>Selected groups, including <i>Vibrio</i> and potentially pathogenic lineages, provide focused case studies within this broader microbiome programme. Detection or gene abundance alone does not establish microbial activity or health risk.</p><h2>Sampling strategy</h2><p>Participating teams coordinate repeated collections of seawater microbes, phytoplankton and zooplankton. The supplied protocol schedules monthly collections, with twice-monthly sampling in the January–April campaign window. Local timing and feasibility are agreed with each station rather than inferred from a single ENSO index.</p><p>Consistent sample identifiers, collection dates, measured coordinates and preservation records link field samples to subsequent DNA extractions. Environmental observations provide context for geographical and seasonal comparisons.</p><p><a class="btn" href="protocol.html">Read the sampling protocol ↗</a></p><h2>Molecular approaches</h2><p>DNA extraction from the collected fractions supports planned metagenomic comparisons of community composition and microbial gene content. Targeted analyses of selected microbial groups can complement the community-wide comparisons. Specific assays and processing steps are agreed through the shared protocol; no unreported sequencing results are presented as project findings.</p><h2>An independent scientific network</h2><p>The initiative connects 30 listed coastal locations across the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian oceans and the Mediterranean Sea. Researchers can propose coordinated sampling in response to exceptional ocean events through the <a href="https://globe-partners.pages.dev/">partner workspace</a>. Participating national networks contribute within this international collaboration.</p></section></div><footer class="site-footer"><div><strong>GLOBE</strong><p>Marine microbiome research.<br>Independent international scientific collaboration.</p></div><p>Project scope: 30 coastal stations · 23 countries<br><a href="../pages/news.html">News</a> · <a href="../pages/resources.html">Sources & resources</a> · <a href="../pages/protocol.html">Sampling protocol</a> · <a href="../pages/privacy.html">Privacy & data use</a> · <a href="../pages/members.html">Partner workspace</a><br>Independent international scientific collaboration</p></footer><script src="../assets/js/site.js?v=20261122-continuous"></script>
